$comment: Primary-source oracle — Roth distribution cases: Pub 590-B §408A ordering with per-year conversion recapture clocks, and the designated-Roth pro-rata split. Expected values derived independently from the cited sources; never from production code.

irs-p590b-ordering.name: IRS Publication 590-B — Ordering Rules for Distributions
irs-p590b-ordering.identifier: Order: (1) regular contributions; (2) conversion/rollover contributions FIFO by year, taxable portion before nontaxable within each year; (3) earnings. Recapture: taxable converted principal withdrawn within its own 5-year period before 59 1/2 is subject to the 10% additional tax (Figuring your recapture amount)

irs-designated-roth-faq.name: IRS — Retirement plans FAQs on designated Roth accounts
irs-designated-roth-faq.identifier: A nonqualified designated-Roth distribution is a pro-rata share of earnings and basis (NOT contribution-first); qualified requires the 5-year period plus age 59 1/2, death, or disability

usc-72t9.name: 26 U.S.C. §72(t) — 10% additional tax; §72(t)(9) governmental 457(b) exception
usc-72t9.identifier: §72(t) reaches a 457(b) distribution only 'to the extent that such distribution is attributable to an amount transferred to an eligible deferred compensation plan from a qualified retirement plan' — ordinary governmental 457(b) amounts are outside the 10% additional tax

cases.description: Nonqualified Roth IRA distribution (owner under 59 1/2) across regular basis, two conversion years (one outside its 5-year window, one inside), and earnings.
derivation: Facts: regular-contribution basis $30,000; conversion lots 2021 (taxable $12,000, nontaxable $3,000) and 2023 (taxable $8,000); first contribution year 2019; distribution year 2026; owner under 59 1/2 -> nonqualified (5-year met but no qualifying event).

Withdrawal $60,000 consumes: 30,000 regular -> 12,000 of 2021 taxable (2026-2021 = 5 >= 5: OUTSIDE the recapture window, no 10% recapture) -> 3,000 of 2021 nontaxable -> 8,000 of 2023 taxable (2026-2023 = 3 < 5: recaptured) -> 7,000 earnings.
Income-taxable = earnings 7,000. 10% additional-tax base = in-window taxable conversion principal 8,000 + pre-59 1/2 earnings 7,000 = 15,000.

cases.description: Qualified Roth IRA distribution (59 1/2 reached AND the 5-taxable-year clock met): entirely tax- and penalty-free.
derivation: Same facts, owner 59 1/2+; first contribution 2019 -> 2026 - 2019 = 7 >= 5 -> qualified.
All buckets still populate for bookkeeping, but income-taxable and additional-tax bases are $0.

cases.description: Nonqualified Roth IRA distribution with a FUTURE-DATED conversion lot (tax year after the distribution year): the future lot cannot exist yet, so the ordering skips it entirely — the shortfall is earnings, not future conversion principal.
derivation: Facts: regular-contribution basis $5,000; conversion lots 2024 (taxable $4,000) and 2027 (taxable $6,000 — dated AFTER the 2026 distribution year); first contribution year 2019; owner under 59 1/2.

Withdrawal $12,000 consumes: 5,000 regular -> 4,000 of 2024 taxable (2026-2024 = 2 < 5: recaptured) -> the 2027 lot is SKIPPED (a conversion in a later tax year is not part of this distribution's facts) -> 3,000 earnings.
Income-taxable = earnings 3,000. 10% additional-tax base = in-window taxable conversion principal 4,000 + pre-59 1/2 earnings 3,000 = 7,000.
Regression guard: an ordering that consumed the future lot would report 7,000 of conversion principal, $0 earnings, and $0 income-taxable — every bucket differs, so a future-lot leak cannot pass.

cases.description: Nonqualified designated-Roth distribution: pro-rata basis/earnings split (NOT contribution-first), earnings taxable + 10% before 59 1/2.
cases.tolerance: exact (pro-rata split after documented half-up integer rounding)
derivation: Account balance $100,000, designated-Roth basis $40,000, withdrawal $10,000; first participation 2023 -> 5-year clock NOT met in 2026 -> nonqualified.

cases.description: Same nonqualified split inside a GOVERNMENTAL 457(b): ordinary Roth 457(b) earnings are exempt from the 10% additional tax (§72(t)(9)); income tax on earnings is unchanged.
derivation: isGovernmental457b -> the earnings leave the 10% base (no rollover-attributable earnings) -> additional-tax base $0; income-taxable stays 6,000.

cases.description: Nonqualified designated-Roth pro-rata split landing EXACTLY on a half-cent: half-up rounding is distinguishable from floor/truncation (a truncating split would report one cent less basis).
cases.tolerance: exact (pro-rata split after documented half-up integer rounding)
derivation: Account balance $120,000, designated-Roth basis $45,000 (ratio 0.375), withdrawal $10,001.00; first participation 2023 -> nonqualified in 2026.

Basis portion = round(1,000,100 * 4,500,000 / 12,000,000) = round(375,037.5) = 375,038 cents (half-up); floor/truncation would give 375,037 — one cent lower, so this case fails under a truncating split.
